lifecycle.label: Archived

purpose.label: Mission

purpose.label: Foundation

pace.description: Expected to change often as needs change

tiers.label: 1 · Mission critical
tiers.description: Care, safety, or the organization's core work stops without it

tiers.label: 2 · Business critical
tiers.description: Important work stops within a day without it

tiers.label: 3 · Business operational
tiers.description: Its loss would be felt within days and worked around

tiers.label: 4 · Administrative
tiers.description: Could be done without for weeks with little effect

tiers.label: 5 · Minimal
tiers.description: Could be switched off with almost no effect

sign_in.description: Organization sign-in and a second factor

sign_in.label: Its own accounts, with multi-factor
sign_in.description: Separate accounts, with a second factor

sign_in.label: Shared accounts
sign_in.description: Accounts or passwords shared between people

sign_in.label: No sign-in
sign_in.description: Open to anyone who can reach it

monitoring.label: None
monitoring.description: Nobody would know it was down until someone said so

monitoring.label: Metrics and logs
monitoring.description: Its health is measured and its logs are kept

monitoring.label: Alerting
monitoring.description: Problems raise an alert to someone

monitoring.label: Alerting to on-call
monitoring.description: Problems reach a staffed on-call rota

backup.label: Unverified
backup.description: Backed up, but a restore has not been tested

backup.label: Tested
backup.description: Backed up, and a restore has been tested

backup.label: Vendor managed
backup.description: The vendor backs it up under its agreement

data_classes.label: Public
data_classes.description: May be shared with anyone: published results, public web content.

data_classes.label: Internal
data_classes.description: Meant for the organization's own work: plans, procedures, most email.

data_classes.label: Personal information
data_classes.description: About identifiable staff, students, donors, or the public.

data_classes.label: De-identified research data
data_classes.description: Research data from which participants cannot reasonably be identified.

data_classes.label: Identifiable research data
data_classes.description: Research data about participants who can be identified.

data_classes.label: Protected health information
data_classes.description: Health information about identifiable patients, held under health privacy law.

data_classes.label: Controlled-access data
data_classes.description: Data received under an agreement that limits who may see it and how.

data_classes.label: Payment card data
data_classes.description: Card numbers and related data, held under the card industry's rules.

radar.label: Hold
radar.description: Not for new work; move away when you can

application_roles.label: Accountable owner
application_roles.description: Answers for it and its record; there is one

application_roles.label: Business owner
application_roles.description: Speaks for the people who use it

application_roles.label: Technical owner
application_roles.description: Answers for how it is built and run

application_roles.label: Support contact
application_roles.description: Whom to call when it is not working

application_roles.label: Data steward
application_roles.description: Answers for the data it holds

external_systems.label: Configuration item
external_systems.description: Its record in the infrastructure inventory

external_systems.label: Sign-in registration
external_systems.description: Its registration with the identity provider

external_systems.label: Contract number
external_systems.description: As the purchasing system knows it

external_systems.label: Governance record
external_systems.description: Its record in another governance system

dispositions.label: Maintain
dispositions.description: Keep it as it is, run efficiently

dispositions.label: Tolerate
dispositions.description: Keep it at the least cost, and look again

dispositions.label: Modernize
dispositions.description: Valuable, but technically weak: upgrade, re-platform, or refactor

dispositions.label: Replace
dispositions.description: The function is needed; this asset should go

dispositions.label: Consolidate
dispositions.description: Does what another application does; move its users there

dispositions.label: Retire
dispositions.description: Little value; retire without a successor

dispositions.label: Incubate
dispositions.description: New or experimental; not yet judged on use

dispositions.label: Assess
dispositions.description: Not enough is known to recommend

fields.label: Ethics protocols
fields.help: The ethics review protocol numbers of the studies that depend on it.

fields.label: Data management plan
fields.help: Where the plan for the data it holds is kept.

fields.label: Accessibility
fields.help: How well people with disabilities can use it, as last checked.

definition.text: An application is software, or a service built from software, that people name, use for a purpose, and could decide to keep, change, or retire as one thing.
examples: A lab's sample tracker, used by three labs
not_examples: A server or a database on its own: record it as a component of what it serves
A report or a module of a larger system: a component of that system
A spreadsheet one person keeps for themselves
A programming language or a platform: a technology
